clue.text: Many at Waterloo let loose, having run into defensive construction

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

indicators.note: into tells us the run abbreviation is placed inside the scrambled letters before they settle
letting something loose frees it from its fixed order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be scrambled
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Troops let loose at the Battle of Waterloo charge into a fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: Martello towers are the small round coastal forts Britain built against Napoleon, which makes the Waterloo setting apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martello tower is a squat round fort built along British coasts as a defence against invasion.

clue.text: Ghastly vehicle and what may have drawn it round

indicators.note: something drawn round another thing encloses it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a horse could have pulled the carriage
a cab is a hired carriage or car

explanation.surface: A grim hearse is described along with the horse that may have pulled it.
explanation.walkthrough: The female horse surrounds the cab: MA-CAB-RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome and death-obsessed, a close synonym of ghastly.

clue.text: Coming up again as needing attention soon after short holiday

indicators.note: short means the word for a holiday loses its final letter

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
something urgent needs prompt attention

explanation.surface: Something keeps returning as a pressing job right after a brief break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the urgent part after the trimmed holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something rising again after a decline, so it is literally coming up again.

clue.text: Run in comfort and wipe out the record

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other word

parts.note: ease is comfort
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes comfortably and then deletes a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside EASE: E-R-ASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase a tape or record is to delete its contents completely.

clue.text: Get escort to deliver this type of fuel

parts.note: to lead someone is to escort them
to deliver from captivity is to free

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a minder along with a fuel delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads deliver as hauling fuel; here it means rescue or set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead-free petrol is unleaded fuel, a common type sold at pumps.

clue.text: Alarm when poison is reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: A warning goes out when news of a poisoning arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, rung to rouse people.

clue.text: Slogan for a hunter, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a motto or rallying cry
second meaning, split in two: the name used for a hunter, a pocket watch with a hinged cover

explanation.surface: A rallying cry used by someone out hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a pocket watch whose lid protects the glass; so the term for it is a watch word.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a motto or guiding slogan adopted by a group or movement.

clue.text: Highland feature good to see during trip

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one item sits inside the other word

parts.note: a ride is a short journey
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A Highland outing offers good views of the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside RIDE: RID-G-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised crest of land, typical of hill country.

clue.text: Fail to break record that's settled

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one word is put within the other

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc record
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: An athlete misses beating a record that now looks fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' tempts as a sporting best, but here it is a disc, and 'Fail' is the piece that breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed matter or case is one that has been decided and finished with.

clue.text: Finishes off can, so save as form of starch

indicators.note: finishing off each word means its ending is cut away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to polish off a tin of food so as to store the starch.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the four words loses its last letter: CA, S, SAV, A. The final 'as' is used twice, as wordplay and linking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava is a tropical root whose starchy flour yields tapioca, so it is a starch source.

clue.text: Constant detail manoeuvring in fortress

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves pieces into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A garrison is kept busy with drill inside the castle walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortified stronghold, often guarding a city.

clue.text: Transported from Pacific island, none the less

indicators.note: read as 'nought the less', it tells us a zero-shaped letter is removed

parts.note: Borneo is a large island, loosely placed in the Pacific

explanation.surface: Someone shipped from a Pacific island regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like 'nevertheless', but it means less an O (nought): BORNEO minus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Borne is the past participle of bear, meaning carried or conveyed.

clue.text: Cows okay in marshes

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: fens are marshy lowlands
right means okay or correct

explanation.surface: Cattle are doing fine out in the wetlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cows' looks like cattle, but it is the verb meaning intimidates; the Fens are the flat wetlands of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to scare them into submission, so cows means frightens.

clue.text: Uplifted and jubilant about day of victory coming round

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jubilant word goes around the other piece

parts.note: elated means jubilant

explanation.surface: Crowds are cheered and jubilant as a victory anniversary comes round again.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day is the anniversary of the 1945 Allied victory in Europe, so 'coming round' suits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means raised up, physically or in spirit, which is what uplifted describes.

clue.text: March following a foolish upset in the plant

parts.note: taken as written
Mar is the calendar abbreviation for March

indicators.note: in a down entry an upset thing is turned upside down, so the foolish word reads backwards

parts.note: silly means foolish

explanation.surface: A procession is followed by a silly disturbance among the greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a verb or the month; it is the abbreviation, and 'upset' suits a down entry, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is a bulbous flowering plant with large trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Fall back on peak, out of energy

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the falling word is read backwards

parts.note: a dip is a fall or drop

explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the reversed fall after TOR: TOR-PID.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, lacking vigour or energy.

clue.text: Individual introducing one small measure to get fruit

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so these pieces go inside the individual

parts.note: a person is an individual
I is the Roman numeral one
mm is the abbreviation for millimetre, a tiny unit

explanation.surface: Someone adds a small quantity of an ingredient to make fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' here means taking the one and the measure inside the individual, not presenting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A persimmon is an orange tomato-like fruit, also called a sharon fruit.

clue.text: Part of the bill for service when eating

clue.text: Servant for Dracula?

second meaning: a man who turns into a bat

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: the vampire Count can take bat form.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is an officer's orderly in the British army, and Dracula is jokingly a man-bat.

clue.text: Turn white as new driver enters the Strand

explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a busy London street, but here strand means shore. L goes inside BEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach is to whiten, or to become pale and lose colour.

clue.text: Company in retreat learning to follow the flag

clue.text: One left note with messenger

explanation.surface: Someone departed after leaving a message with a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One left' means a person left something in a will, not one who went away.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a bequest, someone to whom property is left.

clue.text: Kind of paper to publish after end of broadcast

parts.note: the final letter of broadcast
to issue is to publish

clue.text: Prompt arrival of English leading to drunken ribaldry

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

clue.text: Fish taken by fellow's cast

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the angler's throw that caught the fish, but it is the definition.

clue.text: Many ships move quickly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a navy or a group of vessels

clue.text: A wicked lot getting lit up when match is over?

parts.words: A wicked lot getting lit up when match is over

clue.text: Stout supporter of local origin
